observation_summary: The StringUtils.join method throws a NullPointerException when an element in the input array has a toString() method that returns null, because the code attempts to call .length() on the result of toString() without checking for null.
reasoning_summary: The bug is caused by a missing validation of the result of array[startIndex].toString(). The code assumes that the result of toString() is non-null when calculating the initial capacity of the StringBuilder. Adding a null check for the result of the toString() call (or handling the null case) is a classic validation/checking error.
evidence_used: StringUtils.java:3298: StringBuilder buf = new StringBuilder((array[startIndex] == null ? 16 : array[startIndex].toString().length()) + 1);
StringUtils.java:3383: StringBuilder buf = new StringBuilder((array[startIndex] == null ? 16 : array[startIndex].toString().length()) + separator.length());
Bug report description: StringUtils.join throws NPE when toString returns null for one of objects in collection

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves changing the logic for calculating the buffer size, the root cause is the lack of validation for the return value of toString(), which is a checking issue.
